lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Alberto! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi! Yes, now's good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, that sounds good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay. The heat is getting to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 4 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it! 4 out of 4 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're already doing things to make it easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're really honest with yourself, and that helps.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. I bought spinach and actually used it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This feels really necessary to you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that the late dinners keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know where the day goes. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the vegetables going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the vegetables. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Frozen vegetables count just as much as fresh, and they're cheaper.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Eating together matters to you, maybe even more than the goal.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, getting back to work is why I'm doing this. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 4 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the late dinners made this week harder, you still got 4 days in, and your plan is to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 4 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Jorge. Bye!

tags.note: Heat discomfort; minor, no action needed
Attributes a preference participant did not state
Reasons: health beyond body, enjoys vegetables
Need to act; fear of cancer returning
Feels better about self when sticking to it
Links goal to getting life back
Family eats late; will not eat alone
Reflects movement and desire to continue
Addresses coach as Jorge; participant is Alberto

flags.reason: Verbatim 'Whatever you pick is fine with me' repeated at lines 29, 37, 44; it reads as scripted and ignores the participant's responses.
Participant voiced strong motivation ('I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back'); coach replied with autonomy statement instead of reflecting or affirming it.
'I know I can do it, I did it before' is self-efficacy change talk; no reflection or affirmation given.
Coach attributes a preference ('You'd rather start small') the participant never stated, putting words in their mouth.
Participant addresses coach as 'Jorge' while the participant is Alberto; verify correct name use or identity in the record.

score.summary: The coach covered the full call structure, reviewed the prior goal, set a new goal, planned for barriers, and summarized, with good use of affirmations and some complex reflections. However, the coach repeated a scripted autonomy line three times and missed several clear change-talk statements about fear of recurrence and self-efficacy.
strengths: Line 10 and line 27 affirm the participant's progress and effort clearly.
Line 47 asks permission before offering the frozen vegetable suggestion at line 49, which is MI-consistent.
Line 51 and line 53 reflect the participant's values around family meals and movement with meaning.
Line 61 gives a clear, accurate summary and line 63 sets the next contact.
coaching_tips: At line 29, reflect the change talk ('You feel you have to do something because you don't want the cancer back') rather than replying with an autonomy statement.
Vary the wording at lines 37 and 44; the repeated 'Whatever you pick is fine with me' feels scripted and dismisses the participant's responses.
At line 11, avoid attributing preferences the participant did not voice; use 'It sounds like you want something sustainable' only if they said so.
At line 46, affirm the self-efficacy ('You've done this before and you know you can') and ask what helped then.
